correctness.rationale: The stated Gaussian RBF Runge–Kutta coefficients match primary equations (12) and (15). With \(\tau=\sqrt2/4\), every mesh input \(g(n/N)\) is strictly positive. Writing \(\delta=\lceil N\tau\rceil/N-\tau\in(0,h)\), differentiation yields \(E-\delta^{-2}=h^2\delta^{-6}(8/9-(4/3)\delta^2-\delta^4/h^2)\ge(2h^4)^{-1}\) for every integer \(N\ge4\). The second-stage contribution is \((3h/4)\exp(E-\delta^{-2})\), while the rest of the step and the exact target remain bounded. Thus the positive divergence is proved for infinitely many meshes, not inferred from finite numerical experiments. Embedded verification returned VERIFY_OK 91.

value.rationale: The result makes the bounded-shape assumption substantive: plain \(C^\infty\) regularity, global state Lipschitzness and avoidance of zero-valued mesh inputs do not preclude complete local-consistency failure. It supplies a mesh-uniform positive lower bound of order \(h\exp(1/(2h^4))\), far beyond the routine warning that an adaptive quotient may be undefined exactly at a zero, and motivates explicit shape safeguards.
